subject: Game Theory
title: Reverse Game Theory
description: A 60-second lesson on Reverse Game Theory.

hook.text: Game theory predicts behavior given rules. Mechanism design flips it: what rules produce the behavior you want?

buildup.text: It's engineering for incentives. You design the game so rational players produce the desired outcome.

discovery.text: Leonid Hurwicz pioneered this field, asking: can we build systems where self-interest serves the common good?

twist.text: The trick: make honesty the best strategy. If lying hurts the liar, truth flows naturally through the system.

climax.text: Hurwicz, Maskin, and Myerson shared the 2007 Nobel Prize for laying the foundations of mechanism design.

punchline.text: Don't change people. Change the game.

quiz.question: How does mechanism design differ from game theory?
options: It designs rules to produce desired outcomes
